subproblem.title: Integrable densities on finitely many unit faces define a current: integrability (I) and existence (II)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b), where ι : Fin n → Fin P is arbitrary (no monotonicity is assumed) and b : Fin P → ℤ. Let w : (pairs) → Euclid n → ℝ be such that w_p is Lebesgue integrable on Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} for every p ∈ s. Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 ∈ Euclid P, Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} and E_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}). Then: (I) for every test n-form ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n (a C^∞ compactly supported n-form on Euclid P) and every p ∈ s, the function y ↦ w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) is integrable on Q₁; (II) there is a current D ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n with D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every test n-form ω.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (w : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ), (∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (w p) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), ∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (fun y => w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) ∧ ∃ D : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), D ω = ∑ p ∈ s, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 5.1, displays (27)–(30) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1840–1885). The argument is steps 1–2 of the supplied proof of the selected node dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_integral_current, using its fact (F2) and the operator-norm half of its fact (F1). No monotonicity of ι is used.

Notation.
- n := m + 1 and e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ) ∈ Euclid P.
- Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}.
- For p = (ι, b): Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)} and E_p := (j ↦ e_{ι(j)}).
- For a test n-form ω: h_{p,ω}(y) := ω(Φ_p y)(E_p).
- ‖α‖ denotes the operator norm of a continuous alternating map α.

1. Φ_p is continuous. It is a constant plus the finite sum over j of the maps y ↦ y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Each coordinate y ↦ y_j is continuous (PiLp.continuous_apply), and constants, sums and scalar multiples of continuous maps are continuous (continuous_const.add, continuous_finsetSum, Continuous.smul).
2. h_{p,ω} is continuous. A test form ω is C^∞ (ω.property.1.1), hence continuous. Evaluation at the fixed tuple E_p is a continuous linear map on n-covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ E_p). So h_{p,ω} = (evaluation at E_p) ∘ ω ∘ Φ_p is continuous. In particular it is a.e.-strongly measurable for volume restricted to Q₁.
3. Operator-norm bound. For every n-covector α and every p, |α(E_p)| ≤ ‖α‖ · Π_j ‖e_{ι(j)}‖ = ‖α‖, by ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and ‖e_l‖ = |1| = 1 (PiLp.norm_single). This holds for arbitrary ι.
4. Test forms are bounded. ω is continuous with compact support (ω.property.1.2 : HasCompactSupport ω). So there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for all x ∈ Euclid P (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). By step 3, |h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ C for all y.
5. Proof of (I). Let p ∈ s. By hypothesis w_p is integrable on Q₁. By steps 2 and 4, h_{p,ω} is a.e.-strongly measurable and |h_{p,ω}| ≤ C everywhere. Hence y ↦ w_p(y)·h_{p,ω}(y) is integrable on Q₁ (Integrable.mul_bdd).
6. The linear functional. For ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n put L(ω) := Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·h_{p,ω}(y) dy.
 - Additivity. The coercion of ω + η to a form is the pointwise sum, and evaluation of covectors is additive, so w_p h_{p,ω+η} = w_p h_{p,ω} + w_p h_{p,η} pointwise. Both summands are integrable on Q₁ by (I), so ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω+η} = ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} + ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,η} (integral_add, integral_congr_ae). Summing over p ∈ s gives L(ω + η) = L(ω) + L(η) (Finset.sum_add_distrib).
 - Homogeneity. h_{p,cω} = c·h_{p,ω}, so w_p h_{p,cω} = c·(w_p h_{p,ω}) and ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,cω} = c·∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} (integral_const_mul). Hence L(cω) = c·L(ω) (Finset.mul_sum).
 Thus L : TestFormOn univ n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
7. Uniform estimate. Let A := Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|. Then A ≥ 0, since each integral of a nonnegative function is ≥ 0 (integral_nonneg).
 Claim: if δ ∈ ℝ and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ δ for all x, then |L(ω)| ≤ A·δ.
 - For p ∈ s and every y, step 3 gives |w_p(y) h_{p,ω}(y)| = |w_p(y)|·|h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ |w_p(y)|·δ.
 - The function y ↦ |w_p(y)|·δ is integrable on Q₁ (Integrable.abs, Integrable.mul_const). So |∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω}| ≤ ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|·δ = (∫_{Q₁} |w_p|)·δ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, integral_mul_const).
 - Therefore |L(ω)| ≤ Σ_{p∈s} |∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω}| ≤ Σ_{p∈s} (∫_{Q₁} |w_p|)·δ = A·δ (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs, Finset.sum_le_sum, Finset.sum_mul).
8. Sequential continuity. Let (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} be test forms with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. By definition there is a compact K ⊆ univ with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j. Also, for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on K, where 0 is the zero test form. Use k = 0.
 - Let ε > 0 and δ := ε/(A + 1) > 0. By Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff there is N with dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x) < δ for all j ≥ N and x ∈ K.
 - The coercion of the zero test form is the zero form, so its iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 at x is 0. Also dist(0, a) = ‖a‖ (dist_zero_left) and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). Hence ‖ω_j(x)‖ < δ for j ≥ N and x ∈ K.
 - If x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and ‖ω_j(x)‖ = 0 ≤ δ.
 - So for every j ≥ N we have ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ δ for all x. Step 7 gives |L(ω_j) − 0| ≤ A·ε/(A + 1) < ε, because A ≥ 0 means A·ε < (A + 1)·ε.
 - By Metric.tendsto_atTop, L(ω_j) → 0.
9. Conclusion. The pair ⟨L, step 8⟩ is an element D of GeometricCurrentOn univ n: its two fields are exactly a linear functional on TestFormOn univ n and the sequential continuity at 0 proved in step 8. By construction, D(ω) = L(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every ω; this holds definitionally. Together with (I) from step 5, this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ_p is continuous and evaluation at the fixed tuple E_p is continuous linear, so h_{p,ω}(y) = ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) is continuous.
|α(E_p)| ≤ ‖α‖ (le_opNorm, ‖e_l‖ = 1), and a compactly supported continuous ω is bounded, so |h_{p,ω}| ≤ C.
(I): w_p·h_{p,ω} is integrable on Q₁ by Integrable.mul_bdd.
L(ω) := Σ_p ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} is linear by integral_add and integral_const_mul, using (I).
Order-0 uniform convergence on the common compact K, plus vanishing off K, gives sup_x ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0, hence L(ω_j) → 0. Then D := ⟨L, continuity⟩ satisfies the formula by rfl.

subproblem.title: Mass bound for a current given by integrable densities on coordinate unit faces (Simon (28) and first line of (30), i.e. (34a))
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b), where ι : Fin n → Fin P is strictly increasing and b : Fin P → ℤ. Let w_p : Euclid n → ℝ be Lebesgue integrable on Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} for every p ∈ s. Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 ∈ Euclid P, Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} and E_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}). Let D ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n satisfy D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every test n-form ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n. Then the mass of D, computed with the Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm, satisfies M(D) = D.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (w : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (D : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), (∀ p ∈ s, StrictMono p.1) → (∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (w p) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), D ω = ∑ p ∈ s, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) → D.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∑ p ∈ s, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |w p y|)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 5.1, (28) and the first line of (30) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1840–1880). The argument is step 3 of the supplied proof of the selected node dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_integral_current, together with its fact (F1) (coefficient part).

Notation.
- n := m + 1 and e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ).
- Q₁ := {y : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1}.
- Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ (p.2 i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{p.1(j)} and E_p := (j ↦ e_{p.1(j)}).
- For a test n-form ω: h_{p,ω}(y) := ω(Φ_p y)(E_p).
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

1. Coefficient bound (F1). Let α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n and let I : Fin n → Fin P be strictly increasing.
 - By definition, |α| = √S with S := Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} f(J). Here f(J) := (α(i ↦ EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (J i)))² if J is strictly increasing, and f(J) := 0 otherwise.
 - Every f(J) is a square or 0, so f(J) ≥ 0.
 - Since EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ l = e_l (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), we have f(I) = α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})².
 - By Finset.single_le_sum (nonnegative terms, I ∈ univ), α(e_I)² = f(I) ≤ S. Hence |α(e_I)| ≤ √S = |α| (Real.abs_le_sqrt).
2. Reduction to admissible forms. By definition, D.mass = D.massOn univ = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal(D ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ n univ}. A test form is admissible when its tsupport lies in univ and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x. By sSup_le it suffices to bound ENNReal.ofReal(D ω) for each admissible ω. By ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal it suffices to show D ω ≤ Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p| for each admissible ω.
3. Pointwise bound. Fix an admissible ω and p ∈ s, and let y ∈ Euclid n. Apply step 1 with α := ω(Φ_p y) and I := p.1, which is strictly increasing by hypothesis. Together with admissibility this gives |h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(Φ_p y)) ≤ 1. Hence |w_p(y)·h_{p,ω}(y)| = |w_p(y)|·|h_{p,ω}(y)| ≤ |w_p(y)|·1 = |w_p(y)|.
4. Termwise integral bound. |w_p| is integrable on Q₁ (Integrable.abs of the integrability hypothesis). By step 3 and norm_integral_le_of_norm_le for volume restricted to Q₁, ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} ≤ |∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω}| ≤ ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|. The first inequality is le_abs_self. This inequality needs only the integrable majorant |w_p| and the pointwise bound, not the integrability of w_p h_{p,ω}.
5. Conclusion. By the formula for D and Finset.sum_le_sum, D ω = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p h_{p,ω} ≤ Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|. Hence ENNReal.ofReal(D ω) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|) for every admissible ω. Taking the supremum (step 2) gives M(D) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p|). ∎
proof_key_steps: (F1): |α(e_I)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for strictly increasing I, because α(e_I)² is one nonnegative summand of the defining sum (basisFun_apply, Finset.single_le_sum, Real.abs_le_sqrt).
M(D) = massOn univ is a sSup over admissible ω (|ω(x)| ≤ 1). By sSup_le and ofReal_le_ofReal it suffices that D ω ≤ Σ_p ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|.
For admissible ω, |w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p y)(E_p)| ≤ |w_p(y)| by (F1) with I = p.1.

subproblem.title: The support of a face current lies on the closed faces with nonzero density
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b), where ι : Fin n → Fin P is arbitrary and b : Fin P → ℤ. Let w_p : Euclid n → ℝ be Lebesgue integrable on Q₁ := {y ∈ Euclid n : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} for every p ∈ s. Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 ∈ Euclid P, Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} and E_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}). Let D ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n satisfy D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy for every test n-form ω. Then every x ∈ spt D, where D.support = univ ∖ zeroRegion D (Simon 6.2.11), equals Φ_p(y) for some p ∈ s with ∫_{Q₁} |w_p| ≠ 0 and some y ∈ [0,1]ⁿ (0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (w : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (D : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), (∀ p ∈ s, IntegrableOn (w p) {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), D ω = ∑ p ∈ s, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, w p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) → ∀ x ∈ D.support, ∃ p ∈ s, (∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |w p y|) ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ y : Euclid (m + 1), (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) = x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1840–1910). The argument is step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected node dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_integral_current.

Notation.
- Q₁ := {y : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1} and Cⁿ := {y : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1}.
- Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ (p.2 i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{p.1(j)} and E_p := (j ↦ e_{p.1(j)}), with e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1.

1. Setup by contradiction. Let x ∈ spt D. Suppose that x ≠ Φ_p(y) for every p ∈ s with ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0 and every y ∈ Cⁿ. Put s* := {p ∈ s : ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0} (Finset.filter) and Z := ⋃_{p∈s*} Φ_p(Cⁿ). The assumption says exactly that x ∉ Z.
2. Z is compact.
 - Cⁿ is the image of the compact box Π_i [0,1] ⊆ (Fin n → ℝ) (isCompact_univ_pi, isCompact_Icc) under the continuous map WithLp.toLp 2 (PiLp.continuous_toLp). So Cⁿ is compact (IsCompact.image).
 - Each Φ_p is continuous: it is a constant plus a finite sum of the maps y ↦ y_j • e_{p.1(j)}, and y ↦ y_j is continuous by PiLp.continuous_apply. So Φ_p(Cⁿ) is compact.
 - The finite union Z is therefore compact (Finset.isCompact_biUnion).
 Hence Z is closed and its complement is an open set containing x. So there is r > 0 with ball(x, r) ⊆ Zᶜ (Metric.isOpen_iff applied to IsClosed.isOpen_compl).
3. D vanishes on W := ball(x, r). Let ω be a test n-form with tsupport ω ⊆ W. By the formula, D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} I_p with I_p := ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(E_p) dy. We show I_p = 0 for every p ∈ s, which gives D(ω) = 0 by Finset.sum_eq_zero.
 (a) Case ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| = 0. The function |w_p| is nonnegative and integrable on Q₁ (Integrable.abs), so its zero integral forces |w_p| = 0 almost everywhere for volume restricted to Q₁ (integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg). Then w_p(y) = 0, so the integrand w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) vanishes, for a.e. y ∈ Q₁. Hence I_p = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
 (b) Case ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0. Then p ∈ s*. For y ∈ Q₁ we have 0 < y_i < 1, so y ∈ Cⁿ and Φ_p(y) ∈ Z. Since W ∩ Z = ∅ and tsupport ω ⊆ W, Φ_p(y) ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(Φ_p(y)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). So the integrand is 0 at every y ∈ Q₁, and I_p = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
 Thus D(ω) = 0 for every test form supported in W, i.e. D vanishes on W (GeometricCurrentOn.VanishesOn W).
4. W witnesses x ∈ zeroRegion D.
 - W is open (isOpen_ball).
 - Its closure is contained in closedBall(x, r) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall). That ball is compact because Euclid P is a proper space (isCompact_closedBall). So closure W is a closed subset of a compact set, hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset with isClosed_closure).
 - Trivially closure W ⊆ univ.
 - D vanishes on W by step 3, and x ∈ W because r > 0 (mem_ball_self).
 By definition of zeroRegion D (the union of all open W with compact closure contained in univ on which D vanishes), x ∈ zeroRegion D.
5. Contradiction. But x ∈ spt D = univ ∖ zeroRegion D, so x ∉ zeroRegion D. Therefore the assumption of step 1 is false: there are p ∈ s with ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0 and y ∈ Cⁿ (0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for all i) with Φ_p(y) = x. ∎
proof_key_steps: If not, x ∉ Z := ⋃_{p∈s*} Φ_p([0,1]ⁿ), where s* = {p ∈ s : ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| ≠ 0}.
Z is compact (compact cube, continuous Φ_p, finite union), hence closed; pick ball(x, r) disjoint from Z.
Faces with ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| = 0 contribute 0, since w_p = 0 a.e. on Q₁. Faces in s* map Q₁ into Z, where every test form supported in the ball vanishes. So D vanishes on the ball.
The ball is open with compact closure in univ, so x ∈ zeroRegion D, contradicting x ∈ spt D.
